deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are Grothendieck's preparation notes for his IHES 'laïus' of Nov–Dec 1967, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates and Jussila, in Dix exposés, 1968). Here X_cris is the crystalline site in the characteristic-0 / infinitesimal sense: thickenings without divided powers. The page carries out the Čech–Alexander computation of crystalline cohomology.

Setup (previous page). Take a closed immersion X ⊂ Y over S with Y smooth (or formally smooth) over S. Let Ỹ^{ν+1} = lim_i of the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhoods of X in Y^{ν+1} (fibre product over S, X embedded diagonally); this is the formal completion of Y^{ν+1} along X. Formal smoothness makes the formal schemes Ỹ^{ν+1} cover the final object of the topos. The Čech descent spectral sequence then reads E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(Ỹ^{ν+1}, F)) ⇒ H^*(X_cris, F).

This page.
1. Assume F is quasi-coherent, i.e. the F_{X'} are quasi-coherent. A marginal addition also requires good behaviour with respect to nilpotent immersions X'' ⊂ X'.
2. For any thickening X' one has H^*(X̃', F) = H^*(X'_zar, F_{X'}).
3. Assume X is affine and the Y are smooth affine. Then every Ỹ^{ν+1} is an affine formal scheme, so higher cohomology vanishes. Hence E_2^{pq} = 0 for q ≠ 0, and the spectral sequence degenerates to
   H^*(X_cris, F) ≅ H^*(ν ↦ F(Y^{ν+1}_{/X})).
   This is the cohomology of the cosimplicial module of sections of the crystal on the formal completions along X: the Čech–Alexander complex.
4. For non-affine X, sheafify on X_zar. For U open in X, set F^{(ν)}(U) = lim_i F(U, U(i)^{ν+1}), where U(i) is the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of U in Y^{ν+1}. If V ⊂ Y is an open set inducing U, this is simply F(V^{ν+1}_{/U}).
5. This gives a cosimplicial sheaf 𝓕^• on X_zar. The next page asserts H^*(X_cris, F) ≅ H^*(X_zar, 𝓕^•), with the hypercohomology spectral sequence H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X, 𝓕^{(ν)})).

What it serves: the comparison of crystalline (infinitesimal) cohomology with de Rham-type complexes, made computable through formal completions. It feeds directly into the next page's invariance result: a nilpotent immersion X_0 ⊂ X induces H^*(X_cris) ≅ H^*(X_{0,cris}), since the completions along X_0 and along X coincide.
errors: Step 3 ('H^q of an affine formal scheme with quasi-coherent F vanishes') needs a Mittag-Leffler / lim^1 argument. For crystals it holds because the transition maps F(Y(i+1)) → F(Y(i)) are surjective, as F(Y(i)) = F(Y(i+1)) ⊗ O_{Y(i)}. The note does not spell this out.
The marginal condition 'bien si X'' ⊂ X'' is left vague. It is presumably the crystal / base-change condition needed for the formula F(Ỹ) = lim F(Y(i)) and for step 2.

In characteristic p this naive formal completion is not the right object; the PD envelope is. The construction is correct only for the infinitesimal (char 0 style) site that Grothendieck was treating in 1967.

ideas.what: Computing crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology by the Čech nerve of formal completions of Y^{ν+1} along X, for a smooth embedding X ⊂ Y
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1968, Crystals); Berthelot (1974) and Berthelot–Ogus (1978) for the PD version
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), §4–5

ideas.what: Degeneration of the Čech spectral sequence in the affine case for quasi-coherent crystals
ideas.modern_name: acyclicity of quasi-coherent sheaves on affine formal schemes

ideas.what: Sheafified version: a cosimplicial Zariski sheaf F^{(ν)} on X computing crystalline cohomology for non-affine X
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex as a complex of Zariski sheaves (linearization)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard draft material for the published 1968 'Crystals' lectures (Čech–Alexander computation, affine degeneration, sheafified cosimplicial version). Nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note at top reads approximately 'et simultanément bien si X''⊂X'!'; the plausible reading is 'et similairement bien si X''⊂X'' — uncertain.
Line 2 reads 'supposons de plus X affine, donc les Y lisses affines' (or 'dans les Y lisses affines'); the meaning is X affine embedded in smooth affine Y.
